newsitem.title: USA: Federal judge in Colorado to hold court in prison.
newsitem.headline: Federal judge in Colorado to hold court in prison.

text.p: A federal judge will take the unusual step of conducting a trial inside a Colorado prison Wednesday because the plaintiff is an inmate 100 miles from the nearest federal courthouse.
U.S. District Judge John Kane Jr. said it would be safer, more practical and more efficient for him to hold the trial in prison than to bring the prisoner and guards to federal court in Denver.

The lawsuit has been brought by inmate Richard Robbins, a non-smoker, who is seeking $50,000 in damages. Robbins alleges prison officers forced him to share a cell with a chain smoker, resulting in health problems.
The officers, Bill Reed and Terry Holden, deny the allegations, according to court documents.
A hearing room at the Colorado State Penitentiary in Canon City, Colorado, will be turned into a courtroom Wednesday for the one-day, non-jury trial.

Kane said he will use the occasion to help determine whether federal trials involving inmates routinely will be conducted inside Colorado prisons rather than the traditional practice of having inmates and prison guards travel to the U.S. courthouse in Denver.
"It is uncommon for a (federal) judge to hold a trial in a prison," said a spokesman for the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts in Washington.
